implementation_notes: Swift on Apple platforms can reach the platform's prefetch - _mm_prefetch on x86 Macs via the intrinsics, or the prefetch asm on arm64 - but it is not a first-class Swift API and must be guarded by architecture checks. The idiomatic Swift prefetch is at a higher level: prefetching a table row (Table.prefetchRows), prefetching a Core Data object, or - most idiomatically - warming the next item while the current one is processed. For CPU memory, Swift's value semantics and contiguous Array<T> are the layout answer (an Array of a small struct is contiguous, an array of class references is not). On the OS side, mmap with MAP_POPULATE and madvise are reachable through Darwin/Glibc, and NSURLSession's prefetching configuration is the networking analogue.
idiom_name: _mm_prefetch / arm64 prefetch asm (guarded); Array<T> of small structs for locality; prefetchRows / NSURLSession prefetch for objects and network
pitfalls: There is no first-class Swift prefetch API; _mm_prefetch is x86-Mac-only and the arm64 equivalent is inline asm, both requiring arch guards.
Array of small structs is contiguous and streams; Array of class references is a pointer chase - the layout is the lever.
UITableView/UICollectionView prefetchRows is the idiomatic 'prefetch' on Apple platforms and has nothing to do with CPU cache lines - do not conflate them.
MAP_POPULATE / madvise are the page-level analogue but are Darwin/Glibc specifics and are advice, not guarantees.
